questions.ask: What is your date of birth?
What are the last four digits of the phone number we have on file for you?

hints.day_month_swapped: Could you please say your date of birth again, with the month as a word?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss.
intents.dispute: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product"; a claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is also a dispute.
intents.already_paid: "I already paid": covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
intents.restructure: A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.vague: A vague period such as "next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.
intents.human: A request to speak with a human.

quotes: A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
rules.opening_is_attempt.derivation: Refusing the opening 'today' ask uses an attempt, after which attempt 1 (a different date) is proposed. So the attempts are the proposals after the opening ask, and the opening ask is not attempt 1.

quotes: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: The floor offered after 'too much' is attempt 1 (the floor on attempt 1's date). Attempt 2 then names the floor 'again' on the deadline.

quotes: If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
If it fails, try once more.
Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.
First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.
When the attempts are used up, stop.
the 12th business day after today
the 7th business day after today
A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
rules.deadline_adjust.derivation: Deadlines are counted in business days, so they are always business days. A non-business date can never be moved past the deadline, so the default previous_business_day is kept. Customer-named weekend or holiday dates are moved to the next business day by rule 20, which the not_business_day line handles.

rules.skipped_repeat_counts.assumption: The brief only says 'Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused.' It does not say whether a skipped step uses an attempt, so the engine default applies.

rules.opening_blocks_repeat.assumption: No ladder step is dated today, so the opening ask cannot be repeated by a step. The default applies.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: The brief does not say this. The default applies, and attempt 1 uses the floor via full_or_floor.

quotes: The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
products.floor_pct.derivation: The floor is an account field, not a percentage.

products.floor_round.assumption: The floor is read as given.

products.promise_scale.assumption: create_promise takes the same unit as get_account.

products.promise_round.assumption: There is no rounding of promise amounts.

quotes: If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them.
Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`.

assumptions: Both briefs were given. The spec follows Brief B (Brief A plus up to three products), which also covers one-product calls. Notes are enabled because Brief B rule 8 requires add_note, which replaces Brief A's 'never uses add_note'.
The materials name no currency. 'dollars' is the default.
The brief does not say how often an unclear answer to a payment question is asked again. A non-answer uses a persuasion attempt (rule 30), so max_unclear is omitted.
Callback business_days_only is false. 'Today' is allowed as stated, and the second day is the next business day.

Rule 30 attempt 1 is full_or_floor on the last business day of this week. On that day itself, it is next week's last business day (week_end_today next_week). Attempt 2 (late band only) is the floor on the deadline. The early band has 1 attempt and the late band has 2.
The floor offered after 'too much' is treated as attempt 1 (the engine default attempt_1). Rule 30 says attempt 1 is for the floor once the customer said the full amount is too much.
A date given only as numbers is read as day, month, year (date_order dmy), per rule 11.
days_late outside 1-45 has no rule. bands_outside is omitted, so the engine default (service_error) applies.
The brief does not mention an 'anything else' turn after a promise. The default (ask once) is kept.
When no promise is recorded, the close uses the first non-paid product's reason in get_account order. This matches the engine's default handling order, so outcome_priority and order stay empty.
Rule 1 requires telling the caller that the call is recorded. The opening says 'We record this call' to stay within the wording constraints.
Spoken questions and sympathy wording not prescribed by the brief were written in plain English.
